reasons: Classification is correct: p0133 is a no-hire ('agree not to hire ... any employee of the other party'), reaches all employees plus affiliates, and lacks any general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out — squarely in the rule's walk-away territory, so it fails the fallback on material terms rather than merely falling short of the preferred wording.

The redline reaches the stated fallback precisely: mutual, solicitation-only (with an express statement that hiring is not restricted, killing the no-hire), limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of involvement, with general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs. Deterministic duration and carve-out checks pass.

The failed 'minimal edit' heuristic (0.763 changed-character ratio) is justified here: converting a no-hire into a scoped non-solicit and adding carve-outs necessarily rewrites the sentence; no smaller edit would remove the no-hire and the all-employees scope.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required first-person-plural tone with the [Playbook] prefix, explains what changed and cites the fallback position without lecturing.
Retaining the mutual structure rather than deleting outright is a reasonable, non-overreaching implementation of the fallback and does not disadvantage us.
